title: mi_xmlrpc_ng Module
content_markdown: This module implements a xmlrpc server that handles xmlrpc requests and generates xmlrpc responses. When a xmlrpc message is received a default method is executed.
overview: This module implements a xmlrpc server that handles xmlrpc requests and generates xmlrpc responses. When a xmlrpc message is received a default method is executed.
how_it_works: At first, it looks up the MI command. If found it parses the called procedure's parameters into a MI tree and the command is executed. A MI reply tree is returned that is formatted back in xmlrpc. The response is built in two ways - like a string that contains the MI tree nodes information (name, values and attributes) or like an array whose elements are consisted of each MI tree node stored information.

dependencies_required.name: libxml2
dependencies_required.reason: must be installed before running OpenSIPS with this module loaded

dependencies_required.name: httpd
dependencies_required.reason: must be loaded before this module

exported_parameters.name: http_root
exported_parameters.description: Specifies the root path for xmlrpc requests: http://[opensips_IP]:[opensips_httpd_port]/[http_root]

exported_parameters.name: trace_destination
exported_parameters.description: Trace destination as defined in the tracing module. Currently the only tracing module is **proto_hep**. This is where traced mi messages will go.
exported_parameters.notes: WARNING: A tracing module must be loaded in order for this parameter to work. (for example **proto_hep**).

exported_parameters.name: trace_bwlist
exported_parameters.description:
Filter traced mi commands based on a blacklist or a whitelist. **trace_destination** must be defined for this parameter to have any purpose. Whitelists can be defined using 'w' or 'W', blacklists using 'b' or 'B'. The type is separate by the actual blacklist by ':'. The mi commands in the list must be separated by ','.

Defining a blacklists means all the commands that are not blacklisted will be traced. Defining a whitelist means all the commands that are not whitelisted will not be traced. **WARNING:** One can't define both a whitelist and a blacklist. Only one of them is allowed. Defining the parameter a second time will just overwrite the first one.
exported_parameters.example_code:
...
## blacklist ps and which mi commands
## all the other commands shall be traced
modparam("mi_xmlrpc_ng", "trace_bwlist", "b: ps, which")
...
## allow only sip_trace mi command
## all the other commands will not be traced
modparam("mi_xmlrpc_ng", "trace_bwlist", "w: sip_trace")
...
exported_parameters.notes: WARNING: A tracing module must be loaded in order for this parameter to work. (for example **proto_hep)**.

configuration_examples.title: Example 1.4. XMLRPC request
configuration_examples.description: This is an example showing the xmlrpc format for the “get\_statistics net: shmem:” MI commad: response.
configuration_examples.code:
POST /xmlrpc HTTP/1.0
Host: my.host.com
User-Agent: My xmlrpc UA
Content-Type: text/xml
Content-Length: 216

<?xml version='1.0'?>
<methodCall>
	<methodName>get\_statistics</methodName>
	<params>
		<param>
		<value>
		<struct>
		<member>
			<name>statistics</name>
			<value>
			<array>
			<data>
				<value><string>shmem:</string></value>
				<value><string>core:</string></value>
			</data>
			</array>
			</value>
		</member>
		</struct>
		</value>
		</param>
	</params>
</methodCall>


HTTP/1.0 200 OK
Content-Length: 236
Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8
Date: Mon, 8 Mar 2013 12:00:00 GMT
